cap: The pattern of IgG and IgM sorts a pregnant patient's immune status. IgG alone means immunity and neither means she is susceptible. IgM alone may be a very early infection or a false positive, so IgG is repeated, and IgG that turns positive is a seroconversion that proves a new infection. When both are positive, low-avidity IgG means the infection is recent and high avidity means it is months old.
teach: Use the same grid for toxoplasmosis, rubella, cytomegalovirus and parvovirus B19, where the timing of the maternal infection decides the fetal risk. A first infection in pregnancy is the dangerous one because the mother has no protective IgG to pass on. The newborn side differs: IgG in the infant is borrowed from the mother and reflects her immunity, whereas IgM or a nucleic acid test in the infant proves infection of the fetus.
